title: Assignment moves the value out of the source
statement: Assigning a = b moves the value from b into a, so b is empty or zero afterwards.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: trace the source variable after an assignment
evidence_patterns.signature: reports the source as empty, zero or undefined

example.item:
b = 4
a = b
What is b?

discriminators.vs_slip: Consistent across items; the learner explains that the value 'went into' the other variable. A slip does not empty the source.

vs.prog.var.assignment-links-variables: Linkers keep both variables and couple them; movers empty the source.

conflicts_with.label: Assignment copies a value into a variable at one moment

resolved_by.label: Assignment copies a value into a variable at one moment

sources.citation: Bayman, P., & Mayer, R. E. (1983). A diagnosis of beginning programmers' misconceptions of BASIC programming statements. Communications of the ACM, 26(9), 677-679.
sources.note: LET statements understood as moving a value.

sources.citation: du Boulay, B. (1986). Some difficulties of learning to program. Journal of Educational Computing Research, 2(1), 57-73.

Sorva, J. (2012). Visual Program Simulation in Introductory Programming Education (Doctoral dissertation, Aalto University). Appendix A catalogues introductory programming misconceptions from the literature.

provenance.notes: Drafted from the cited literature for the OML seed pack; statement, examples and discriminators are original text. Awaiting maintainer review.
